source.title: G-Mix: A Generalized Mixup Learning Framework Toward Flat Minima

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure values are garbled or unavailable in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size and measures test accuracy and the training–test gap, using a different experimental setup from the claim version's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports batch-size sweeps for six methods on STL-10 and Cifar-100; exact curve values are available only in figures. Its other method comparisons and rho/gamma ablations concern Mixup/SAM combinations and are not covered by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The batch-size sweep measures held-out accuracy for WRN-16-4 on STL-10 and CIFAR-100 under several training methods. The stated default budget is 200 epochs for both datasets, and no exception is given for this sweep. These accuracy results test V5, although the extracted rows record only a different measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct: the authors conclude that G-Mix and its BG-Mix and DG-Mix extensions improve generalization in their tested image-classification settings, and report declining best test accuracy and their Gap metric as batch size increases. They also report greater batch-size robustness for their proposed algorithms. Their Gap is test accuracy minus training accuracy, with larger values treated as better.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Mixup and SAM-based training and measures test accuracy and a training–test gap in image classifiers; the paper does not reproduce the claim versions' random-label, architecture, optimizer, dropout, or sharpness-measurement experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the reported test accuracy and gap trends; the study also varies rho and gamma, but those ablations concern its proposed methods and do not test a listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: The batch-size rows measure the best signed difference between test and training accuracy. A decline in this quantity cannot independently establish a decline in test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size lowers the paper's best test-minus-training accuracy metric in the tested WRN settings.

fits_no_version.finding: G-Mix, BG-Mix, and DG-Mix are compared with Vanilla, SAM, and Mixup for accuracy, the signed accuracy difference, and computation cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining Mixup with SAM and sensitivity-based example handling improves image-classification accuracy in the tested settings.

record.problems: Batch-size sweep outcomes are shown in figures without recoverable numerical values in the text; results are limited to image-classification datasets and the paper's stated training setup.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Table I, Table II, Figs. 2–3 and rho/gamma ablations compare methods or parameters but do not test a listed claim version; their results are not catalog rows for those versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error; WRN versus ResNet-18 does not isolate width or interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, switching optimizers, and decoupled weight decay.

Language models, longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization changes, and removal of the penalty within the same epoch budget. The batch-size threshold and uncertainty are not established.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

missing.what: Six best-test-accuracy batch-size sweep rows for Vanilla, SAM, Mixup, G-Mix, BG-Mix, and DG-Mix on STL-10. The authors explicitly state that accuracy decreases with batch size; exact individual curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Fig. 4(a); Section V-C, Impact of Batch Size; Section V-B, Training Details

missing.what: Six corresponding accuracy sweep rows on CIFAR-100. Mixup decreases from 77.89% to 70.25%, a 7.64 percentage-point decline. The text also gives 78.67% to 74.57% for a proposed algorithm, a 4.10 percentage-point decline, but does not identify which proposed algorithm in that sentence; do not assign it without readable figure evidence.
missing.locator: Fig. 4(c); Section V-C, Impact of Batch Size, page 15

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly marks fixed-epoch comparisons as untested: Section V-B specifies 200 epochs for both sweep datasets, with no sweep-specific change stated. Best accuracy is selected during training rather than measured only at the final epoch. The existing Gap rows cannot support the accuracy verdict. No uncertainty is reported for the sweep.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and related tuning or weight-decay conditions.
Language models; fixed-epoch comparisons as specified in the version; longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization changes, and same-epoch matching cases.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a predictor of the gap, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: WRN-16-4 on STL-10 and CIFAR-100, batches 32–512, Vanilla, SAM, Mixup, G-Mix, BG-Mix, and DG-Mix; stated default 200-epoch budget
relationships.reason: Based on the text and missing accuracy rows, not R1–R12: Section V-C explicitly reports declining best test accuracy as batch size increases across the compared methods. On CIFAR-100, Mixup falls from 77.89% to 70.25%.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports declining best test accuracy across the compared methods as batches increased, but these comparisons remain unverified.
